matchstick.title: Move vertical I-stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: If the numeric discrepancy can be fixed by adding or removing a value of 1, move a single vertical stick from one numeral to another to adjust the values accordingly.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is off by exactly one and there is an I (vertical stick) that can be moved without breaking character validity.
matchstick.example: Attempting to fix a discrepancy of 2 by moving a vertical stick, which cannot change the value by 2.

matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: First try to fix the equation by moving a stick within the same character (e.g., turning X into V) before considering moves between characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick move within a character can produce a valid new character and potentially correct the equation.
matchstick.example: Skipping an intra-character transformation like X→V and directly moving a stick to another numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, ensure every resulting character is a recognized Roman numeral or operator; discard transformations that produce invalid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Leaving a single diagonal stick alone, which does not correspond to any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A single diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; angled sticks must appear in valid pairs (e.g., V or X).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a move would leave an isolated diagonal stick or create a character with only one angled stick.
matchstick.example: Removing one diagonal from X and not repositioning it, leaving a stray diagonal.

matchstick.title: Convert plus to minus by removing vertical stick
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into a minus sign.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and you need a '-' while preserving the moved stick for reuse elsewhere.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' but forgetting to place it, leaving an orphan stick.

matchstick.title: Create new numeral by reordering stick
matchstick.principle: A detached stick can be placed as a separate character to form a new valid Roman numeral (e.g., moving a vertical stick to create an additional I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the moved stick can serve as a standalone numeral without breaking existing characters.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick but placing it in a location that does not form a recognizable numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra‑character move yields a valid equality, explore moving a stick from one character to another to form new numerals or operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra‑character options without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from one numeral to another but ending up with an invalid character on the source side.

matchstick.title: Augment numeral with vertical stick from operator
matchstick.principle: After converting a plus sign to a minus by removing its vertical stick, attach that stick to a nearby numeral to increase its value (e.g., turning I into II).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you have a '+' that can be turned into '-' and the freed vertical stick can improve a numeral.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' and discarding it instead of adding it to an I.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: After forming new Roman numerals and operators, compute their numeric values to ensure the equation holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After a candidate transformation passes symbol validation.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that yields 12 = 9 - 12 without checking that the RHS is negative.

matchstick.title: Preserve exactly one equals sign after stick move
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=' operator; if the original '=' is altered, the moved stick must be used to create a new '=' elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from the '=' sign or any operator that could affect the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=' to turn it into '-' and not placing that stick elsewhere, resulting in an equation without an '='.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tends to jump to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler fixes within a single character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate all possible intra‑character stick relocations that keep the character valid before considering inter‑character moves.

matchstick.description: Assuming sticks retain their orientation and not rotating horizontals to verticals (or vice versa) when repositioning
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable regardless of direction, ignoring the rule that orientation is fixed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When moving a stick, keep its original orientation; a vertical stick must remain vertical, a diagonal must remain diagonal, and a horizontal must remain horizontal.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often stops after finding a syntactically valid arrangement, forgetting to check if the numeric equality holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after a transformation and verify the equality before accepting the answer.

matchstick.description: Assuming operator swaps (e.g., converting '=' to '-' or vice versa) automatically solve the puzzle, without ensuring a single '=' remains
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model believes that swapping operators will balance the equation, overlooking that the equation must still contain exactly one equality sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When altering operators, verify that the final equation still has exactly one '=', and that the new operators produce a correct arithmetic balance.

matchstick.description: Forgetting to place the removed stick after modifying an operator (e.g., converting plus to minus) and leaving it unused
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes treats the removed stick as discarded rather than repositioned, violating the one‑stick‑move rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the removed stick and explicitly decide where to attach it, ensuring the total stick count remains unchanged.
